overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data clearly highlights that space, extreme planetary conditions, and 'What If' scenarios dominate engagement velocity. Specifically, videos published around late September and early October (such as Venus's day/year anomaly, liquid diamond planets, and the darkest planet TrES-2b) significantly outperform older September titles in daily views and engagement ratios (likes-per-view).

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on bizarre planetary mechanics like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views), 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1029 views), and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1030 views) generate the highest views and strong like-to-view ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-concept cosmic anomalies and speculative physics ('What If') regarding lesser-known celestial bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Why Your Head Is Older Than Your Feet' (265 views) performed notably well for a mid-September release, proving audience appetite for counter-intuitive scientific realities.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form concepts based on relativity, quantum quirks, or biological anomalies that challenge daily perceptions.

weak_patterns.pattern: Standard Animal Trivia without a High-Concept Hook
weak_patterns.evidence: General animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (when repeated or framed simply) and standard memory tricks showed stagnant or much lower overall view velocities compared to cosmic phenomena.
weak_patterns.action: Shift away from simple trivia statements about animals unless tied to a shocking evolutionary mystery or a cinematic survival/what-if angle.
